text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Barrick to inherit Bre-X riches: Indonesia wields sword over Calgary firm in high-stakes negotiations for gold ownership.
- Canada reduces mission scale: Awaiting approval of food air drops.
- Canadian Airlines, 4 unions request $35 million: Workers to match government 'relief'
- Quebec faces public-sector strike: Six unions form common front to oppose government's attempts to cut salaries.
- Convicts get out on own reference: Auditor deplores lack of release data.
- Ball clubs back deal with players.
- Bank of Montreal joins billion-dollar club: Third-biggest bank's profit cracks 10-figure mark by 'firing on all cylinders,' Barrett says.
- Peter Munk nears top of gold heap: Winning control of Bre-X's Indonesian deposit would vault the entrepreneur's Barrick Gold to first place among the world's producers.
- Wage cut alone won't save Canadian Airlines, analysts agree: Payroll savings a drop in the bucket; airline must overhaul route structure.
- Expectations build for interest rate cut: Foreigners' T-bill buying may pave way.

- Indonesia squeezes Bre-X into Barrick's grasp: Indonesian government orders Bre-X to put 75 percent of its gold bonanza into Barrick's hands by Dec. 4 and says it would also 'appreciate' a piece of the action.
- Alberta leads charge to keep Canadian flying.
